claim: A request that sends any non-empty totpCode together with a valid backupCode skips the password check (line 121) and then passes 2FA through the backup-code branch, so email plus one backup code is enough to log in without the password.

Consuming a backup code is a non-atomic read-decrypt-modify-write, so concurrent logins with the same code all succeed and the 'single-use' guarantee is lost; concurrent use of different codes can also resurrect a consumed code (lost update).

On the new DisplayBackupCodes step 2FA is already enabled server-side, but closing the dialog via Escape/overlay goes through onOpenChange, which never calls onEnable() or resetState(), so the settings switch keeps showing 2FA as disabled and the modal reopens stuck on the backup-codes step.

Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have backupCodes = null and there is no way to generate codes short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA; exhausted code lists (all null) are reported as IncorrectBackupCode rather than MissingBackupCodes.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] No way to generate or regenerate backup codes for existing or exhausted users

**Severity:** LOW — the feature does nothing for every user who already has 2FA, and gives a misleading error once all codes are used.

### The Problem
Codes are created only in `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, and that endpoint refuses users who already have 2FA (`TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`). The migration `20230804153419_add_backup_codes` adds a nullable column and does not backfill it. So every user who already has 2FA gets:
```ts
if (!user.backupCodes) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes); // line 137
```
Used codes are replaced with `null` (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and never removed. After ten uses the array is `[null x10]`, which is truthy, so the user gets `IncorrectBackupCode` ("wrong code") and not `MissingBackupCodes`.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The "Lost access" button shows for every 2FA user, but it can never work for anyone who set up 2FA before this deploy. That is the group most likely to need it. Users who use up all ten codes are told their code is wrong.

### Research
GitHub, Google and Okta all offer "Regenerate recovery codes" (which requires re-authentication) and warn when few codes are left.

### Recommendation
- Add a password-protected `/api/auth/two-factor/backup-codes/regenerate` endpoint and a settings button that shows the same backup-codes screen.
- Treat an exhausted list the same as a missing one:
```ts
if (!user.backupCodes) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes);
const backupCodes: (string | null)[] = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, KEY));
if (backupCodes.every((c) => c === null)) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes);
```

claim: The object URL holding the plaintext backup codes is never revoked on close/cancel/unmount (resetState does not revoke it and backupCodes state is never cleared), so the codes remain retrievable from the page for its lifetime.
